elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Rendered 7.2 now reads "Customer may engage any other provider at any time and has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation to Vendor," deleting the prior disclose-and-match gating (right of first refusal) that operated as de facto exclusivity; retained 12.3 independently confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," and no other requirements or sole-supply obligation on Customer remains in the cited text.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no exclusivity obligation binds Customer at all (7.2 as rendered plus 12.3), so there is no exclusivity requiring category limitation; the stricter preferred outcome subsumes this element.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity period exists after deletion of the disclose-and-match gate; 7.2 permits engaging any other provider "at any time," so there is no duration to cap.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no exclusivity to terminate; Customer's sourcing freedom is unconditional and not tied to Vendor performance.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation survives, so no delivery-date-based exit is needed; 7.2 grants an unconditional right to engage other providers.

reasons: The edit is confined to Section 7.2, the single operative source of the de facto exclusivity (mandatory disclosure and matching of competing offers before engaging another provider), and does not touch Section 2.1 (minimum volume), Section 12.4 (non-compete) or any other commercial mechanic.

Replacing rather than merely striking 7.2 is acceptable as a concise insertion: it avoids leaving an empty numbered subsection and adds only the words needed to state the preferred position; the mild overlap with the Vendor acknowledgment in 12.3 is confirmatory, not contradictory, and creates no competing operative standard.
No extras were added — no survival tail, remedy, procedure, notice mechanic or damages language beyond the single checklist element.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, and retained 12.3 now aligns with 7.2 instead of being contradicted by it; pricing, term and service-level mechanics elsewhere are untouched.

Both levels are position-complete — the preferred element is met on its face, and the fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because no exclusivity obligation remains to be limited, timed or terminated.
